title: Chapter 5 Mastery Quiz: The Rise of Behaviorism
description: Demonstrate comprehensive mastery of Pavlovian conditioning, Watson's manifesto, Skinner's operant technology, and biological limits.

questions.question: For what scientific discovery did Ivan Pavlov win the Nobel Prize in 1904?
questions.explanation: Pavlov received the 1904 Nobel Prize for his physiological research on digestive secretions.

questions.question: In Pavlov's classical conditioning experiments, what was the meat powder placed in the dog's mouth?
questions.explanation: The meat powder naturally and automatically triggered salivation without training, making it the Unconditioned Stimulus.

questions.question: What process occurs when a conditioned stimulus is repeatedly presented alone without the unconditioned stimulus, causing the conditioned response to gradually diminish?
questions.explanation: Extinction is the weakening and eventual disappearance of a learned response when the CS is no longer paired with the UCS.

questions.question: What is 'spontaneous recovery' in classical conditioning?

options.text: The sudden reappearance of an extinguished conditioned response after a rest interval
The rapid healing of a brain lesion
The immediate extinction of a phobia upon first exposure
The recovery of conscious memory under hypnosis

questions.explanation: Spontaneous recovery refers to the return of an extinguished conditioned response following a delay without retraining.

questions.question: A dog conditioned to salivate to a 1000 Hz tone also salivates slightly to an 800 Hz tone. What phenomenon does this illustrate?
questions.explanation: Stimulus generalization is the tendency for stimuli similar to the CS to evoke similar conditioned responses.

questions.question: What was the landmark title of John B. Watson's 1913 Columbia University lecture that launched Behaviorism?

options.text: Psychology as the Behaviorist Views It
The Reflex Arc Concept in Psychology

questions.explanation: Watson delivered his historic 'Psychology as the Behaviorist Views It' lecture in 1913, establishing the school of Behaviorism.

questions.question: In the Little Albert experiment (1920), what served as the Unconditioned Stimulus (UCS)?

options.text: The loud clanging noise from striking a steel bar

questions.explanation: The loud, frightening acoustic noise created by striking the steel bar naturally induced fear, serving as the UCS.

questions.question: How did Little Albert demonstrate stimulus generalization after fear conditioning?

options.text: He showed fear toward other white, furry objects like rabbits, dogs, and a Santa mask
He refused to eat any solid food
He became terrified of loud music only
He refused to look at books

questions.explanation: Albert generalized his fear of the white rat to a white rabbit, dog, fur coat, and cotton beard.

questions.question: What famous boast did John B. Watson make regarding the power of environmental conditioning over heredity?

options.text: 'Give me a dozen healthy infants... and I'll guarantee to train any one to become any type of specialist'
'The unconscious mind cannot be influenced by conditioning'

questions.explanation: Watson asserted extreme environmentalism, boasting that he could shape any healthy infant into a doctor, lawyer, artist, or thief through conditioning.

questions.question: What apparatus did Edward Thorndike construct to study trial-and-error learning in cats?
questions.explanation: Thorndike used custom-built wooden puzzle boxes with latches, pulleys, and treadles to study learning in cats.

questions.question: What does Edward Thorndike's 'Law of Effect' state?

options.text: Responses accompanied or closely followed by satisfaction are more likely to recur
All learning requires insight and mental problem-solving
Sensations must be categorized into elements

questions.explanation: The Law of Effect posits that behaviors producing satisfying outcomes are stamped in, while those producing discomfort are stamped out.

questions.question: How does Operant Conditioning differ fundamentally from Classical Conditioning?

options.text: Operant conditioning focuses on voluntary behaviors influenced by consequences; Classical conditioning pairs involuntary reflexes with stimuli
Operant conditioning uses no food or rewards
Classical conditioning only works on humans
Operant conditioning relies exclusively on introspection

questions.explanation: Classical conditioning links involuntary autonomic reflexes to antecedent stimuli; operant conditioning shapes voluntary emitted behaviors through consequences.

questions.question: What is the defining characteristic of Negative Reinforcement?

options.text: Removing an unpleasant stimulus to strengthen a desired behavior
Delivering an electrical shock to punish bad behavior
Ignoring behavior until it undergoes extinction
Taking away a toy to stop a child from fighting

questions.explanation: Negative reinforcement increases behavior frequency by terminating or escaping an aversive stimulus (e.g. taking aspirin removes a headache).

questions.question: A parent confiscates their teenager's driver's license for breaking curfew, reducing the likelihood of breaking curfew again. What operant contingency is this?
questions.explanation: Removing a valued stimulus (driver's license) to decrease unwanted behavior is Negative Punishment.

questions.question: Which schedule of reinforcement produces the highest and most steady rates of responding, and is most resistant to extinction (e.g. gambling)?
questions.explanation: Variable Ratio reinforcement delivers rewards after an unpredictable number of responses, creating powerful, compulsive persistence.

questions.question: What behavioral method did B.F. Skinner use to teach complex behaviors by reinforcing successive approximations toward a target goal?
questions.explanation: Shaping (differential reinforcement of successive approximations) trains novel complex behaviors step-by-step.

questions.question: What 1948 utopian novel did B.F. Skinner publish portraying a society engineered entirely through positive operant reinforcement?
questions.explanation: Skinner's novel 'Walden Two' depicted an intentional community flourishing through behavioral engineering and positive reinforcement.

questions.question: In psychiatric hospitals and schools, what name is given to reinforcement systems where patients earn tokens exchangeable for rewards?
questions.explanation: A token economy uses secondary conditioned reinforcers (tokens) that can be exchanged for primary or backup reinforcers.

questions.question: What groundbreaking finding did John Garcia establish that violated the traditional behaviorist principle of equipotentiality?

options.text: Rats readily associate taste with nausea even with hours of delay, but cannot easily associate sound with nausea
Animals can never be conditioned with food rewards
Conditioning only works under bright sunlight

questions.explanation: The Garcia Effect demonstrated biological preparedness: evolutionary survival mechanisms dictate which stimuli can be readily paired.

questions.question: What phenomenon did Keller and Marian Breland discover in 'The Misbehavior of Organisms' where animals revert to innate instincts despite operant training?
questions.explanation: Instinctive drift is the tendency of learned operant behaviors to gradually drift back toward innate, biological behavioral patterns.

questions.question: What therapeutic approach pioneered by Ivar Lovaas relies on operant conditioning principles to treat autism spectrum disorders?
questions.explanation: Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) uses operant reinforcement and shaping to develop language, academic, and social skills in autistic individuals.

questions.question: What was Behaviorism's greatest overarching impact on the discipline of psychology?

options.text: It established strict operational definitions, objective measurement, and methodological rigor across all psychology
It proved that thinking and emotions do not biologically exist
It eliminated the study of genetics in psychology

questions.explanation: Behaviorism transformed psychology into an objective science by enforcing precise operational definitions and empirical laboratory measurement.
